name: Belém Tower
text: Iconic 16th-century fortified tower on the Tagus river, a symbol of Portugal's Age of Discovery and a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Jerónimos Monastery
text: Vast Manueline-style monastery in Belém with ornate cloisters, one of Lisbon's most impressive landmarks.

name: Time Out Market
text: Lively food hall where top Lisbon chefs and vendors serve everything from fresh seafood to pastries under one roof.

name: Tram 28
text: Historic yellow tram that winds through Alfama, Graça and Baixa, a classic way to see the old city's steep streets.

name: Alfama District
text: Lisbon's oldest neighbourhood, a maze of narrow lanes, viewpoints and fado houses below São Jorge Castle.

name: Pastéis de Belém
text: The original custard-tart bakery, serving warm pastéis de nata from a secret recipe since 1837.

name: Louvre Museum
text: The world's largest art museum, home to the Mona Lisa and tens of thousands of works; best visited early to beat the crowds.

name: Eiffel Tower
text: Paris's defining iron landmark with observation decks; stunning at sunset and when it sparkles on the hour after dark.

name: Le Marais
text: Historic district packed with falafel stands, bakeries, cafés and boutiques, great for a relaxed food stroll.

name: Musée d'Orsay
text: Beaux-Arts railway station turned museum with the world's finest collection of Impressionist masterpieces.

name: Montmartre
text: Hilltop artists' quarter crowned by the Sacré-Cœur basilica, with winding streets and sweeping city views.

name: Seine River Cruise
text: Boat trip past Notre-Dame, the Louvre and the Eiffel Tower, a scenic way to see the monuments from the water.

name: Colosseum
text: Ancient Roman amphitheatre that once held 50,000 spectators; book a timed ticket to skip the long lines.

name: Vatican Museums
text: Immense museum complex ending at the Sistine Chapel's Michelangelo ceiling; go early or late to avoid crowds.

name: Trastevere
text: Cobblestoned neighbourhood famed for trattorias and nightlife, ideal for an evening of classic Roman cuisine.

name: Pantheon
text: Remarkably preserved ancient temple with the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome and an open oculus.

name: Trevi Fountain
text: Baroque masterpiece and Rome's most famous fountain; tradition says a tossed coin ensures your return.

name: Roman Forum
text: Sprawling ruins of the political and commercial heart of ancient Rome, next to the Palatine Hill.

name: Sagrada Família
text: Gaudí's extraordinary unfinished basilica with soaring tree-like columns and kaleidoscopic stained glass.

name: Park Güell
text: Whimsical Gaudí park of mosaic terraces and organic architecture with panoramic views over the city.

name: La Boqueria Market
text: Bustling covered market off La Rambla with tapas bars, fresh juices, jamón and seafood counters.

name: Gothic Quarter
text: Medieval maze of narrow streets and plazas around the cathedral, full of history, shops and cafés.

name: Barceloneta Beach
text: City beach with a lively boardwalk, water sports and seafood chiringuitos, a short walk from the old town.

name: Casa Batlló
text: Gaudí's fantastical modernist house on Passeig de Gràcia, with a scaled roof and bone-like balconies.

name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
text: Shinto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred Mount Inari; go early for quiet photos.

name: Kinkaku-ji
text: The Golden Pavilion, a Zen temple covered in gold leaf reflected in a tranquil mirror pond.

name: Nishiki Market
text: Narrow five-block market known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen', lined with stalls selling street food, pickles and sweets.

name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
text: Ethereal path through towering bamboo stalks, best paired with the nearby Tenryu-ji temple and river.

name: Gion District
text: Kyoto's historic geisha quarter of wooden machiya teahouses, atmospheric at dusk along Hanamikoji Street.

name: Kiyomizu-dera
text: Hillside Buddhist temple with a vast wooden stage offering sweeping views, especially in cherry-blossom and autumn seasons.
